payload.title: Santorini Wedding Packages and What They Include
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning a Santorini wedding for guests flying in from Australia. They have a shortlist of Santorini venues and are now holding package documents that share a name but not a shape: one bundles a ceremony set-up and coordinator, another sells use of a terrace for set hours, a third expects a planner to bring the rest. They want to know what a Santorini venue package really covers, what sits outside it, and how to put two quotes side by side before they pay a deposit.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can compare the couple's shortlisted Santorini venue packages like for like, with the quote in AUD and inclusions confirmed in writing.
payload.angle: Santorini wedding packages look alike in a search result and differ on paper. Page-one results list prices and adjectives; this guide shows, only from what each Santorini venue publishes about its own package, what sits inside (ceremony set-up, coordinator, spaces and hours), what is charged on top or left to the couple (guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours, outside suppliers, documents), and where a venue package ends and a planner begins. It turns those gaps into a like-for-like quote checklist an Australian couple can take into any proposal. No figures, so the comparison stays true when prices change.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: a Santorini venue package usually bundles the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a space, while guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours and outside suppliers vary by venue; link /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues prominently in the intro.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one sentence, no figures.

Types of package: ceremony-only, ceremony and reception bundles, named tiers, exclusive-use or space hire, elopement or packages for two, each tied to a Santorini venue that publishes it (venue names allowed only where their package is described), in fresh wording.
What packages include: each inclusion attributed to the venue that states it, written plainly without research talk.

What is left out or charged on top, written as questions to ask, only where a venue says so ('a fee applies' or 'charged on top' only where the source says so): exclusive use, guest rooms and minimum nights, extra hours, outside suppliers and supplier rules, documents.

Ceremony type inside a package: religious, civil and symbolic as venues state them; one short legal line (Smartraveller and Embassy Athens facts as at November 2026; 'check with the Municipality of Thira and the embassy, including any fees'); link /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding for the steps; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once. Nothing implies the Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork.
Venue fee vs package vs planner: practical trade-offs, no planner or vendor names.

Comparing two quotes like for like: checklist (ceremony type, guest count basis, spaces and hours, exclusive use, rooms and nights, supplier rules, documents, currency, deposit and cancellation terms), no figures; the single body Advisor line follows it.
Australian angle: is the quote in euros or AUD (as a question); deposit and cancellation terms as questions; travel insurance only as a question.

One Advisor line in the body plus the close, from brand-facts.md only: one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, inclusions confirmed in writing before the couple commits.

Links: /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding-venues (prominent), /destination-weddings/santorini-wedding (prominent), /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-wedding-packages (only if SEO confirms live and relevant), /destinations/europe/greece, /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions (once), /wonderland-concierge with UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=santorini-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing, /magazine. Anchor text says 'Wedded Concierge', never 'Wonderland Concierge'.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD amount, 'from' price or percentage anywhere, including FAQ, meta and alt text.

Research talk ('on its own site', 'in its own words', 'does not publish' as our search, page dates as source talk, myths sections); 'often told' more than once; hedge stacking; linking any source more than once.
'Best' claims, best month, ranking packages; calling a package all inclusive unless the venue says so.
Stating a legal meaning not in an official source; any Advisor role in legal, church or religious paperwork.
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; Wedded Privileges; transfer arrangements; 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance' (note brand-facts.md wording contains it: do not reuse).
Planner or other vendor names; venue contact or business details; implied partnerships or preferred rates.
Competitor sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Em dashes, US spelling, exclamation marks, clichés, keyword-stuffed headings.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; unlicensed images.
Repeating the venues guide's venue profiles or the planning guide's legal steps; summarise and link instead.

SEO to confirm rankings for santorini wedding packages and variants (all inclusive, cost, elopement package, packages for 2).
payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's real problem (two Santorini package documents that look alike but are not), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, then link the Santorini venues guide and the planning guide.
key_takeaways_plan: A Santorini venue package usually covers the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a space, and the rest depends on the venue.
Guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours and outside suppliers are where Santorini packages differ most, so ask about each in writing.
A venue package, a venue fee and a planner each cover different ground, so check who is responsible for every part of the day.
Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before paying any deposit.
